title: Logarithmic descent time: D(n) = O(log n)
statement: Let D(n) = min { k >= 1 : J^k(n) < n } be the first-descent time. Then sup_{n >= 2} D(n) / log n < infinity. Quantitative form of juggler_asymptotic_descent; implies it with an explicit certificate-length bound K(n) = c log n.
tested_range: record table of the [2, 2000000] census in data/research/juggler/above_anchor_walk/summary.json: max D = 257 at n = 1122603; D/ln n at successive record holders grows slowly (13.3 at 193, 22.4 at 78901, 18.4 at the final record) - consistent with O(log n) up to a slowly varying factor, inconclusive on strict boundedness; the sqrt(n log n) envelope scale is far above every record (ratio falls from 2.75 to 0.065)
notes: The walk heuristic predicts descent within O(sqrt(n log n)) steps if floor defects at near-minima were bounded below; the observed records are drastically smaller and track c log n, consistent with parity behaving quasi-randomly (each prefix has a fixed chance of going exponent-negative). A proof at any rate f(n) = o(n) would already give eventual descent. Not a claim.
